text: for anything on the billing service, I'm the owner — ping me. currently mid-refactor of the invoicing flow.
and I own payments + core infra (Stripe integration, webhooks, the deploy pipeline).
I'm on the on-call rotation this quarter with Miguel. incident escalations come to us first.
data + the events service is me. if you need anything on analytics or the event schema, that's my area.
notifications service is stuck — a bunch of emails never went out overnight. looks like the queue consumer died and messages piled up with no retry.
added a dead-letter queue + retry-with-backoff so a single bad message can't block the whole consumer. backfilled the missed ones.
prod was down ~20 min. the payment webhook was silently dropping retries after we bumped the Stripe timeout last week. no error surfaced, just missing confirmations.
oof. so the retries were being swallowed? how'd you catch it?
yeah. fixed it by adding idempotency keys on the webhook handler so retries are safe and don't get deduped away. confirmations are flowing again.
nice. can you write that up in the incident doc? this'll bite us again otherwise.
reminder: standup moved to 10am on Fridays.
anyone up for lunch at the Thai place?
out on PTO next week, back the 9th. Miguel covering on-call.
proposal: move the events service off Postgres to MongoDB. our event payloads keep changing shape and the migrations are painful. flexible schema would help us move faster.
I'm wary. we lean on transactions for the events->billing handoff. losing strong consistency there scares me.
billing definitely needs consistency on that handoff. but if events itself is append-mostly, Mongo could be fine for just that service.
decision: we'll move ONLY the events service to MongoDB, keep billing on Postgres. revisit in a month.
the office coffee machine is broken again 😭
Project Falcon kickoff: goal is self-serve onboarding so new customers can set up without sales. target GA end of Q3.
Falcon update: billing side of self-serve is done in staging. blocked on the events service refactor before we can wire usage metering.
kudos to Dev for the DLQ fix back in April, saved us during last night's traffic spike.
🙏 the backoff logic is holding up nicely.
update on the Mongo move: we've hit consistency headaches on the events->billing sync, exactly what I worried about. duplicate and out-of-order events.
agreed it's not worth it. decision reversed: we're moving the events service back to Postgres and using JSONB for the flexible payloads. best of both.
good call. JSONB gives us the schema flexibility without giving up transactions.
Falcon: now that events is back on Postgres, usage metering is unblocked. picking it back up this week.
heads up: bumping the Stripe API version next sprint. will re-verify the webhook idempotency handling before we ship.
Falcon risk: GA date is tight. if metering slips past mid-Aug we should push GA to early Q4.
